text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Service r-hosted-1 experiencing elevated 95/99p latency and increased 500s. Autoscaler is oscillating (multiple scale events in last 10m). Investigate ASAP.

shelley: on it. paging rajiv and kevin. @rajiv can you take initial triage? we need scope (customer impact + root cause signals).

rajiv: ack. looking at metrics now — CPU stable but KV cache entries for model-x have shot up ~x6 in last 8m. continuous_batcher queue length spiked.

kevin: seeing repeated scale up/down logs on nodes-gpu-asia-*. HPA events every ~90s. probable warmup/thrash loop.

anika: adding some telemetry: logs show many short-lived requests causing tiny prefixes to be cached then evicted -> cache keeps growing with low reuse. continuous batching window default=250ms might be too aggressive under this traffic pattern.

shelley: that matches symptom: cache blowup increases memory/CPU on runtime which triggers HPA, which then drains cold nodes and causes more batching warmups -> thrash.

rajiv: attaching snippet from runtime logs (tail):

```
2026-03-15T21:11:02Z runtime INFO kv_cache.size=12840 model=model-x
2026-03-15T21:11:03Z runtime WARN continuous_batcher.window_ms=250 inflight=180 queued=240
2026-03-15T21:11:04Z hpa INFO scale.up to 12 replicas (cpu 78%)
2026-03-15T21:11:12Z runtime INFO kv_cache.size=34102 model=model-x
2026-03-15T21:11:14Z hpa INFO scale.down to 6 replicas (cpu 22%)
```

kevin: oof. we should mitigate quickly with config hotfix: 1) lower continuous_batcher.window_ms to 80-100ms; 2) add cache eviction cap per-model; 3) increase HPA stabilization window to prevent oscillation.

anika: agree. propose patch (small change) — doing a rolling patch to dedicated pool r-hosted-1. patch:

```
# rollout-hotfix: reduce continuous batch window and soft cap cache
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: runtime-tuning
data:
  continuous_batcher.window_ms: "100"
  kv_cache.soft_limit_per_model: "16000"
  hpa.scale_down_stabilization_seconds: "240"
```

shelley: if we apply that, we should also prewarm top prefixes to avoid cold-miss storm while nodes settle. can we run lightweight prewarm for top-5 prefixes?

rajiv: yes. will run a prewarm job against 3 replicas to populate KV and warm KV cache for model-x.

kevin: /me patching now.

kevin: `kubectl apply -f runtime-hotfix-176120.yaml -n r-hosted-1`

kevin: output: `configmap/runtime-tuning configured` -> initiating rolling restart of runtime pods (graceful) :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Deployment r-hosted-1-runtime rollout started by kevin (rollout-id=rl-176120-1).

shelley: starting prewarm job: `jobs/prewarm-top-prefixes --model=model-x --replicas=3 --rate=50/s` — will report progress.

rajiv: prewarm logs show prefix hit rate climbing from ~2% to 48% within 90s. KV cache growth rate dropped significantly.

anika: HPA events suppressed after stabilization window change. scale events reduced, nodes stable at 8 replicas.

support-squad: heads up — earlier customer-facing errors between 21:10-21:18 UTC. impacted ~7 enterprise customers with elevated 5xx and latency. We're preparing comms now. No data loss.

shelley: good. timeline so far: alert 21:10 -> triage 21:11 -> patch applied 21:18 -> prewarm + stabilization 21:22 -> metrics back to normal by 21:30.

kevin: action items for now:
- monitor KV cache size for model-x and model-y for next 3 hours
- leave continuous_batcher.window_ms=100 for 24h then re-evaluate
- run synthetic traffic test at low rate to validate no thrash
- support to send incident note to affected customers

rajiv: quick note: we should add circuit to continuous_batcher to disable long-window batching when cache growth crosses threshold. filing a follow-up RFC.

shelley: acknowledged. I'll take the oncall for the next 2 hours and then handoff to kevin. if anything regresses ping me directly and escalate to SRE-ENG.

kevin: copy. I'll be online for handoff at 23:15 UTC.

support-squad: sending out customer notice: drafted note: "We experienced elevated latency and errors on model inference due to a caching and batching interaction; mitigations applied and performance normalized. No customer data was lost. Contact support if you see continued issues." sending at 21:40 UTC.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: ALERT RESOLVED (auto): metrics returned within SLOs. mark incident as mitigated. Incident ID: INC-20260315-001.

shelley: will create postmortem with timeline + root cause + follow-ups (tuning + circuit + e2e test) and tag eng-runtime, eng-infra, product. Drafting now.

rajiv: adding follow-ups:
- implement per-model soft eviction and hard eviction fallback
- add telemetry to alert when kv_cache.growth_rate > X per min
- run stress tests that simulate many short prefix patterns

shelley: ok team. great coordination. closing thread after handoff.

kevin: thanks all. :thumbsup:
